title: Developer
subtitle: API keys, MCP connections, usage and audit log.

usage.noneBody: Requests made with API keys or MCP connections will be counted here.

scopes.dangerNotice: Dangerous scopes let this key act on live accounts or remove data. Grant them only when you need them.

posts_write.label: Create and edit drafts
posts_write.description: Create drafts, edit and cancel posts.

media_write.label: Upload media
media_write.description: Upload files to the media library.

posts_publish.label: Publish immediately
posts_publish.description: Publish to live social accounts right now.

posts_delete.label: Delete posts
posts_delete.description: Delete posts from Steerpost. Published copies stay on the networks.

social_connect.label: Connect accounts
social_connect.description: Hand a network credential (token, app password, webhook URL) to Steerpost. Anyone holding this key can attach accounts.

trusted.label: Trusted key: do not ask me before dangerous actions.
trusted.hint: By default, dangerous actions by this key wait for your approval in Approvals.
trusted.warning: A trusted key acts without asking. If it leaks, or the agent misbehaves, it can publish to your live networks, delete posts and disconnect accounts straight away. Leave this off unless the key runs unattended.
trusted.ack: I understand this key can publish, delete and disconnect without my approval.

apiKeys.rawBody: This is the only time the full key is shown. Store it somewhere safe.
apiKeys.ackRequired: Confirm that you understand the risk of dangerous scopes.
apiKeys.trustAckRequired: Confirm that this key may act without your approval, or turn the trusted option off.
apiKeys.createBody: Keys act as you. Grant only what the integration needs.
apiKeys.ackDangerous: I understand this key can ask to publish, delete or disconnect. Each request waits for my approval.
apiKeys.intro: Use API keys for scripts and integrations. Send as {header}
apiKeys.emptyBody: Create a key to call the REST API from your own tools. To connect an AI agent, <link>use an MCP connection</link>.
apiKeys.revokeBody: Anything using “{name}” stops working immediately. This cannot be undone.

mcp.createdBody: This config contains the API key and is shown only once. Paste it into your MCP client now.
mcp.httpIntro: Native HTTP with an Authorization header. In Claude Code run the one-liner below; in Cursor put the JSON into mcp.json and replace the key with {envKey} if you keep it in an environment variable.
mcp.connectorIntro: Connector (no install): add a custom connector with your MCP URL and the header {header}. The URL must be reachable over HTTPS. Steps: MCP docs.
mcp.bridgeIntro: Bridge: paste this into claude_desktop_config.json and restart Claude Desktop. It runs the community package mcp-remote pinned to an exact version; the key stays in the env block, not in the command line.
mcp.nameRequired: Give the connection a name, e.g. “Claude Desktop”.
mcp.ackRequired: Confirm that you understand the risk of dangerous permissions.
mcp.approvalNotice: Publishing, deleting and disconnecting wait for your approval in Approvals, every time.
mcp.ackLabel: I understand and want to grant these permissions.
mcp.emptyBody: Create a connection above, then paste the config into your MCP client.
mcp.revokeBody: “{name}” loses access immediately and its API key stops working.

read.label: Read posts
read.description: Agents can list accounts, posts, statuses and analytics.

draft.label: Create drafts
draft.description: Agents can create and edit drafts with media you uploaded.

schedule.label: Schedule
schedule.description: Agents can schedule posts to publish later.

publish.label: Publish
publish.description: Agents can publish to live accounts immediately.
